MetricDefinition.description: Simple custom metric: name has 1..200 characters; eventNames has 1..100 validated names; aggregation is count, unique_count, sum, average or percentile. Percentile requires a finite quantile strictly between zero and one, using exact inclusive (R-7) interpolation on finite Float64 samples; empty groups emit no point. Quantile is forbidden for other aggregations and ratio components. Sum/average/percentile require a numeric aggregationProperty declared across every listed event. Filters are grammar strings: at most eight AND groups, each with up to eight OR terms and 16384 decoded UTF-8 bytes combined with request filters. groupBy uses up to two distinct full dimension names. Day is the default grain; request grouping/grain override saved defaults. No SQL is accepted.

group.description: Full dimension names map to scalar text or null. Empty string and null are distinct.

MetricResult.description: A complete aggregate answer with at most 10000 points. Larger answers return the permanent metric_result_too_large problem; no partial result or cursor pages are returned.

RatioMetric.description: Ratio of two simple definitions; component grouping must be empty and timeGrain null. Each side supports count, unique_count, sum or average and its own filters. Request filters apply to both sides within each population's eight-group/16384-byte budget. Ratios are unbucketed, reject event-property grouping and return zero for a zero denominator. Names are labels, never builtin dispatch keys.

Legacy measures reject the list. Rates use the selected first-session population, not legacy users. Conversions may come from any source in the range at or after session start. includeBots controls whole sessions and individual conversion events. user_id is filter-only: eq/neq accept one nonempty opaque string; in accepts 1..20 raw string IDs before deduplication (1024 UTF-8 bytes each). Existing route grains, populations, budgets and 10000 complete-point cap apply; selecting one user is not a keyed lookup. Canonical user timelines ordered by millisecond occurred_at then event_id, with immutable duplicates removed. At most 20 steps; one event cannot satisfy repeated steps. mode=any_order opens one window at the earliest matching step and counts distinct step positions; mode=sequential (default) allows intervening events; strict requires adjacency including automatic events, accepts current-user filters over complete participant timelines, and rejects event filters. counting=uniques (default) selects maximum reach, earliest completion, earliest start, then event IDs for sequential/strict. counting=totals counts nonoverlapping entries, restarting after completion, expiry or interruption; any-order entries start at any step, others at step one. Totals add an ungrouped measure=entries point per variant and label reach rows measure=count. There is no exclusion grace period. window is inclusive seconds from first step, default range capped at 7776000. Repeat exclude up to 20 distinct validated names; exclusions between matched steps stop a chain, and cannot overlap steps. measure=count (default) emits cumulative reach. time_to_convert emits exact nearest-rank p50_seconds/p90_seconds for reached steps >=2, from the same selected chain. One/two group dimensions use the earliest eligible start (per attempt for totals). prop attribution=first_touch (default), last_touch or step:<n> uses the start, last matched event or named step; absent/unreached values are other. Validate declarations in that step, or compatible declared properties across steps when touch varies; user dimensions use participant current traits. Sequential event filters select step rows and cannot hide exclusions. Positive half-open range at most 366 days; native execution/memory limits; at most 10000 complete points or HTTP 400. Per-variant timelines include only events at or after that user/variant first exposure inside the range. Multi-variant users remain in each variant.

Nested session dimensions and other routes are excluded.aggregate=users (default) or organizations merges member timelines and excludes empty organization IDs. The organizations route always counts organizations. attribution=event (default) preserves event organization IDs; user_organization fills only missing IDs from the resolved user current group membership. Current org:plan, org:industry, org:country and numeric org:seats traits reclassify historical reports. Experiments retain user aggregation. See Organisations in the query guide.
